zeugma.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ζεῦγμα (zeûgma, “yoking; a bond, a band”), from ζεύγνυμι (zeúgnumi, “to yoke; to join”), from ζεῦγος (zeûgos, “a yoke”).

s.d: use of a verb with two or more complements, playing on the verb's polysemy, for humorous effect
x: ‘Mr. Pickwick took his hat and his leave’ is an example of zeugma

s.d: (uncountable) The act of using a word, particularly an adjective or verb, to apply to more than one noun when its sense is appropriate to only one.
(uncountable) Syllepsis.
x: The existence of zeugmas suggests the rule of transitivity. Zeugmas appear incorrect because they embody an allegedly univocal use of a term in a way which violated^([sic]) the rule of transitivity.
